notes: Identity verified internally against the neutral reference: title Standing enhances cognitive control and alters visual search; authors Kendra C. Smith, Christopher C. Davoli, William H. Knapp III, Richard A. Abrams; DOI 10.3758/s13414-019-01723-6; Attention, Perception, & Psychophysics (2019) 81:2320–2329. Supplied canonical text is a full primary research article with three experiments, methods, results, discussion and references, not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied (source_pdf_path null); no acquisition or PDF rendering performed. Experiment 3 candidate response-time tests on p.2326: set size F(1, 11) = 81.9, p < .001, ηp2 = .88; posture × set size F(1, 11) = 5.9, p = .033, ηp2 = .35; posture F < 1. Search-rate sign test p = .039 is separate. Accuracy set size F(1, 11) = 3.4, p = .09; posture F < 1; posture × set size F(1, 11) = 7.96, p = .017 (no partial eta-squared printed for that accuracy interaction). No target selected. Participant-count candidate: 12 participants reported in Method; within-subjects design reported, but participation count is not explicitly labelled final critical-model analytic N. No analytic N calculated from df, and no mutually exclusive final groups summed. The neutral locator identifies an experiment/page and multiple terms or a broad performance construct, without uniquely identifying outcome (accuracy versus response time) and ANOVA term.
